This appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short " MV Act") has been filed challenging the award dated 28.02.2017 passed by Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Raipur (CG) in Claim Case No.422/2015.

entities.text: Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Raipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By the impugned award, the learned tribunal has awarded Rs.2,42,000/- as compensation to the appellants/claimants with 7.5% interest per annum on account of injury sustained by appellant/claimant in an unfortunate accident which took place on 04.04.2015 by rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle i.e. Indica Car bearing Registration No. C.G. 15/CE-8300 by respondent No.1/driver and owned by respondent No.2/owner.

2) The claim application was filed inter alia pleading that because of accident occurred, the appellant/claimant suffered severe injuries including permanent disablement and she remained in hospital for a considerable period of time and award is on the lower side.
Neutral Citation 3) The claim application was resisted by respondents/driver and owner of the offending vehicle on various grounds.

4) The learned tribunal on the basis of pleadings of the parties framed issues and after appreciation Ku. Anku Verma vs Daya Ram Dhangar on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104145181/
1 of evidence and material available on record awarded the compensation as stated above.
5) Learned counsel for appellants/claimants submits that looking to the injury sustained and period of hospitalization, the amount of compensation is on the lower side, therefore, it may suitably be enhanced.
6) Learned counsel for respondent No.1 supported the award and submits that no treating doctor was examined neither any disability certificate was filed, the claim with regard to treatment and on other heads is genuine.

entities.text: Anku Verma vs Daya Ram Dhangar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7) Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the record with utmost circumspection.

8) The tribunal has awarded compensation in the following manner:-
1. Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-.
2.Special Diet Rs.10,000/-.
3.

Conveyance Charges Rs.5,000/-
4. Attendant Charges Rs.10,000/-.

5. Medical Expenses Rs.1,65,000/-.
6.
Miscellaneous expenses Rs.2,000/-.
9) Admittedly, no treating doctor was examined neither any disability certificate was filed.
The amount claimed with regard to treatment has already been awarded and the amount on other heads also appears to be reasonable and just.
Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, there is no scope for en hancement of compensation.
10) The appeal fails and is dismissed.

Sd/-
